Electricity Troubleshooting Guide:
Power Outage in the Apartment: Locate the apartments electrical panel (Stromkasten), it is located in the entrance behind the glass wardrobe. Open the panel door to access the switches. Check for any switch that is down or tripped. Use the legend sticker to identify the affected area. Once identified, flip the switch back up to reset it. The outage may have been caused by a specific device, such as a microwave or hairdryer. Try identifying the faulty device by plugging and unplugging devices, as either the plug or the device itself may need repair or replacement. (Overloading can also cause a power loss, in that case unplug devices from the affected area.) Report the damage to the office maintenance team!

The circuit breaker trips frequently, causing a power outage in a specific area: Too many devices on one circuit can overload it. Unplug some devices and reset the breaker. Devices like microwaves, heaters, or hairdryers can easily overload a circuit. Avoid using them all at once. If the breaker continues to trip after reducing the load, report it for inspection.

Lights Flickering: Report it to the maintenance team for a more in-depth inspection.

A specific electrical device, like a microwave or TV, isn’t functioning: Plug the device into a different outlet to ensure the problem isn't with the outlet. If the device still doesn’t work after trying other outlets, it may need to be repaired or replaced. Report the issue to the maintenance team for further investigation.

A specific light or outlet is non-functional: Test the outlet by plugging in another device. If the outlet isn’t working, check the breaker. If the breaker has tripped, reset it as described above. If the issue remains unresolved, report it to the maintenance team for professional help.

You smell burning or see smoke near an outlet, switch, or appliance: Immediately shut off the general power supply by flipping the switch in the electrical panel (Stromkasten) for the affected area - it is located in the entrance behind the glass wardrobe. Disconnect any devices from the outlet or switch where the smell or smoke is coming from. Avoid using the outlet or appliance until it has been inspected. Report the issue immediately to the maintenance team for urgent inspection and repair.

No Signal or No Picture on the Screen: Check that the TV is powered on (indicator light should be lit). Make sure the correct input source is selected (HDMI 1, HDMI 2, etc.) using the Input/source button on the remote.

Remote Not Working: Ensure there are no obstructions between the remote and the TV’s sensor. Try using the TV’s physical buttons to control it. Replace the batteries in the remote if required.

No Sound: Increase the volume using the TV remote. Check if the TV is muted (look for a mute icon on the screen or remote).

Streaming App Issues (e.g., Netflix, YouTube): Check that the TV is connected to WiFi. Alternatively try restarting the app/TV by closing and reopening it.

Electricity Troubleshooting Guide:
Power Outage in the Apartment: Locate the apartments electrical panel (Stromkasten), it is located in the entrance GET DATA [GET DATA]. Open the panel door to access the switches. Check for any switch that is down or tripped. Use the legend sticker to identify the affected area. Once identified, flip the switch back up to reset it. The outage may have been caused by a specific device, such as a microwave or hairdryer. Try identifying the faulty device by plugging and unplugging devices, as either the plug or the device itself may need repair or replacement. (Overloading can also cause a power loss, in that case unplug devices from the affected area.) Report the damage to the office maintenance team!

The circuit breaker trips frequently, causing a power outage in a specific area: Too many devices on one circuit can overload it. Unplug some devices and reset the breaker. Devices like microwaves, heaters, or hairdryers can easily overload a circuit. Avoid using them all at once. If the breaker continues to trip after reducing the load, report it for inspection.

Lights Flickering: Report it to the maintenance team for a more in-depth inspection.

A specific electrical device, like a microwave or TV, isn’t functioning: Plug the device into a different outlet to ensure the problem isn't with the outlet. If the device still doesn’t work after trying other outlets, it may need to be repaired or replaced. Report the issue to the maintenance team for further investigation.

A specific light or outlet is non-functional: Test the outlet by plugging in another device. If the outlet isn’t working, check the breaker. If the breaker has tripped, reset it as described above. If the issue remains unresolved, report it to the maintenance team for professional help.

You smell burning or see smoke near an outlet, switch, or appliance: Immediately shut off the general power supply by flipping the switch in the electrical panel (Stromkasten) for the affected area - it is located in the entrance behind the glass wardrobe. Disconnect any devices from the outlet or switch where the smell or smoke is coming from. Avoid using the outlet or appliance until it has been inspected. Report the issue immediately to the maintenance team for urgent inspection and repair.

Electricity Troubleshooting Guide:
Power Outage in the Apartment: Locate the apartments electrical panel (Stromkasten), it is located next to the entrance door. Open the panel door to access the switches. Check for any switch that is down or tripped. Use the legend sticker to identify the affected area. Once identified, flip the switch back up to reset it. The outage may have been caused by a specific device, such as a microwave or hairdryer. Try identifying the faulty device by plugging and unplugging devices, as either the plug or the device itself may need repair or replacement. (Overloading can also cause a power loss, in that case unplug devices from the affected area.) Report the damage to the office maintenance team!

The circuit breaker trips frequently, causing a power outage in a specific area: Too many devices on one circuit can overload it. Unplug some devices and reset the breaker. Devices like microwaves, heaters, or hairdryers can easily overload a circuit. Avoid using them all at once. If the breaker continues to trip after reducing the load, report it for inspection.

Lights Flickering: Report it to the maintenance team for a more in-depth inspection.

A specific electrical device, like a microwave or TV, isn’t functioning: Plug the device into a different outlet to ensure the problem isn't with the outlet. If the device still doesn’t work after trying other outlets, it may need to be repaired or replaced. Report the issue to the maintenance team for further investigation.

A specific light or outlet is non-functional: Test the outlet by plugging in another device. If the outlet isn’t working, check the breaker. If the breaker has tripped, reset it as described above. If the issue remains unresolved, report it to the maintenance team for professional help.

You smell burning or see smoke near an outlet, switch, or appliance: Immediately shut off the general power supply by flipping the switch in the electrical panel (Stromkasten) for the affected area - it is located next to the entrance door. Disconnect any devices from the outlet or switch where the smell or smoke is coming from. Avoid using the outlet or appliance until it has been inspected. Report the issue immediately to the maintenance team for urgent inspection and repair.

Radiator Making Noise: Report it to the maintenance team for further inspection.

The radiator stays hot even when turned off: Ensure the valve is fully turned counterclockwise to the "0" position. If the radiator remains on, report it to the maintenance team for professional repair.

Water is leaking from the radiator: Turn Off the Radiator by turning the valve counterclockwise to stop the water flow. Use a towel or container to catch any leaking water. Report the issue to the maintenance team for urgent repair.

The radiator is hot, but the room isn’t warming up: Ensure windows and doors are fully closed to prevent drafts. Make sure no furniture or curtains are blocking the radiator, preventing heat circulation. Adjust the valve to a higher setting to increase heat output. If the room remains cold, report it to the maintenance team for further inspection.
